stem: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as main product while AgCN forms isocyanides as the chief product. Explain.
solution: KCN is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C—C bond is more stable than C—N bond. However, AgCN is mainly covalent in nature and nitrogen is free to donate electron pair forming isocyanide as the main product.

stem:
In the following pairs of halogen compounds, which would undergo \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) reaction faster?

(i) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\) (chloromethylcyclohexane) and \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}\) (chlorocyclohexane)

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}\) (1-iodobutane) and \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\) (1-chlorobutane)
solution:
(i) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\) — it is a primary halide and therefore undergoes \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) reaction faster.

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}\) — as iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size, it will be released at a faster rate in the presence of incoming nucleophile.
_note: The book prints both members of each pair as DRAWN structures: pair (i) as a cyclohexane ring bearing \(\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\) and a cyclohexane ring bearing \(\text{Cl}\); pair (ii) as two skeletal zig-zags. The chain length of pair (ii) was counted from the PDF's own vector paths (four carbon vertices in each), so both are n-butyl.

stem:
Predict the order of reactivity of the following compounds in \(\text{S}_\text{N}1\) and \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) reactions:

(i) The four isomeric bromobutanes

(ii) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\), \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br}\), \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{Br}\), \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br}\)
solution:
(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} < (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3 < (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\) (\(\text{S}_\text{N}1\))

\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\) (\(\text{S}_\text{N}2\))

Of the two primary bromides, the carbocation intermediate derived from \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}\) is more stable than derived from \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) because of greater electron donating inductive effect of \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\) group. Therefore, \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}\) is more reactive than \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) in \(\text{S}_\text{N}1\) reactions. \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3\) is a secondary bromide and \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\) is a tertiary bromide. Hence the above order is followed in \(\text{S}_\text{N}1\). The reactivity in \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) reactions follows the reverse order as the steric hinderance around the electrophilic carbon increases in that order.

(ii) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br} > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br} > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{Br} > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) (\(\text{S}_\text{N}1\))

\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br} < \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br} < \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{Br} < \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\) (\(\text{S}_\text{N}2\))

Of the two secondary bromides, the carbocation intermediate obtained from \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br}\) is more stable than obtained from \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{Br}\) because it is stabilised by two phenyl groups due to resonance. Therefore, the former bromide is more reactive than the latter in \(\text{S}_\text{N}1\) reactions. A phenyl group is bulkier than a methyl group. Therefore, \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Br}\) is less reactive than \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{Br}\) in \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) reactions.
_note: The stem is printed at the foot of printed p.174 (p-15) and its whole solution overleaf on p.175 (p-16); both halves are transcribed here.

stem:
Identify chiral and achiral molecules in each of the following pair of compounds. (Wedge and Dash representations according to Class XI.

(i) (i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{OH}\)  (ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHBr}_2\)

(ii) (i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (pentan-2-ol)  (ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (pentan-3-ol)

(iii) (i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)  (ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}\)
solution:
The chiral molecule in each pair is the first one:

(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{OH}\) — its carbon carries four different groups \((\text{H},\ \text{CH}_3,\ \text{Br},\ \text{OH})\). Its partner \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHBr}_2\) carries two identical bromine atoms and is achiral.

(ii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (pentan-2-ol) — C-2 carries \(\text{H}\), \(\text{OH}\), \(\text{CH}_3\) and \(\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\). Its partner pentan-3-ol carries two identical ethyl groups on the carbinol carbon and is achiral.

(iii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) (2-bromobutane) — C-2 carries \(\text{H}\), \(\text{Br}\), \(\text{CH}_3\) and \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\). Its partner 1-bromobutane is achiral.
_note: TWO printed features preserved. (1) The stem's parenthesis is never closed — the book prints "(Wedge and Dash representations according to Class XI." with no closing bracket; transcribed as printed. (2) The book's printed SOLUTION consists of three drawn structures and no words at all: it answers by drawing only the CHIRAL member of each pair, leaving the achiral partner implicit. The reasons given above are supplied to make the row usable; the identifications themselves are the book's. Pairs (i) and (ii) are printed as wedge-and-dash structures and pair (ii) as skeletal chains; the carbon counts were confirmed against the PDF vector paths and against the book's own solution drawings.

stem: Although chlorine is an electron withdrawing group, yet it is ortho-, para- directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions. Why?
solution:
Chlorine withdraws electrons through inductive effect and releases electrons through resonance. Through inductive effect, chlorine destabilises the intermediate carbocation formed during the electrophilic substitution.

Through resonance, halogen tends to stabilise the carbocation and the effect is more pronounced at ortho- and para- positions. The inductive effect is stronger than resonance and causes net electron withdrawal and thus causes net deactivation. The resonance effect tends to oppose the inductive effect for the attack at ortho- and para- positions and hence makes the deactivation less for ortho- and para- attack. Reactivity is thus controlled by the stronger inductive effect and orientation is controlled by resonance effect.
_note: The book's solution also prints three resonance schemes (inductive destabilisation of the carbocation, and attack at the ortho- and para- positions) between the two paragraphs transcribed here; the prose carries the full argument.
